1	=== docs/how-callisto-works.md
2	 1 │ # How Callisto works
3	 2 │ 
4	 3 │ Callisto turns changesets and native package metadata into a version plan. It then coordinates the selected registry, Git, and GitHub operations. Current scope is Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI.
5	 4 │ 
6	 5 │ ## Where it fits
7	 6 │ 
8	 7 │ Use Callisto when contributors should declare release impact and a repo needs native dependency updates across its supported package types. The version plan makes each bump reviewable before publication.
9	 8 │ 
10	 9 │ Other tools may fit your existing workflow:
11	10 │ 
12	11 │ - [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) focuses on npm package releases.
13	12 │ - [Knope](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) offers configurable release workflows.
14	13 │ - [Nx Release](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases) integrates with Nx projects and tasks.
15	14 │ - [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/design.md) builds release PRs from conventional commits.
16	15 │ 
17	16 │ ## A change through the system
18	17 │ 
19	18 │ Suppose a Cargo crate `service` depends on `core`. A contributor records a change to `core`:
20	19 │ 
21	20 │ ```sh
22	21 │ callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API"
23	22 │ callisto status
24	23 │ callisto version --dry-run
25	24 │ ```
26	25 │ 
27	26 │ Callisto builds the version plan from the changeset, manifests, and `callisto.toml`:
28	27 │ 
29	28 │ - The changeset requests a minor bump for `core`.
30	29 │ - The Cargo dependency in `service` tells Callisto whether the new version fits its existing requirement.
31	30 │   - Under the default `out-of-range` policy, a version outside that requirement can bump `service` and update its dependency declaration.
32	31 │   - Cascade mode and bump severity are configurable.
33	32 │ - Fixed and linked groups can add packages through explicit policy.
34	33 │ - Unrelated npm and Python packages do not join solely because they share the repo.
35	34 │ 
36	35 │ After reviewing the plan, `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs. It stages the versioned state for a commit. `callisto release --dry-run` then previews the release operations.
37	36 │ 
38	37 │ ## The model
39	38 │ 
40	39 │ | Concept | What it means today |
41	40 │ | --- | --- |
42	41 │ | Workspace package | A dependency graph node located from source and manifests. |
43	42 │ | Distribution | A native Cargo, npm, or PyPI identity described by a manifest. One package can expose multiple supported distributions. |
44	43 │ | Native dependency | A manifest relationship that can affect dependent versions and publication order. |
45	44 │ | Version group | An explicit fixed or linked rule in `callisto.toml`. |
46	45 │ | Release operation | One registry, tag, GitHub release, or asset effect with prerequisites. |
47	46 │ 
48	47 │ These relationships serve different purposes. For example, a Rust library embedded in a Python wheel is a build input. That alone does not create a Cargo registry dependency or make the crate and wheel share a version. See [configuration](config.md) for supported dependency and version-group rules.
49	48 │ 
50	49 │ ## Releasing and recovery
51	50 │ 
52	51 │ - **Local release:** `callisto release --dry-run` previews the plan. `callisto release` runs it from a clean checkout.
53	52 │   - Native publishers use their own credentials.
54	53 │ - **Managed CI:** The version PR commits the selected package and version decision. CI verifies it after merge.
55	54 │   - Planning declares operations. Building creates artifacts. Execution receives registry credentials.
56	55 │ - **Execution:** Callisto checks each provider before acting.
57	56 │   - It adopts an exact match, performs and confirms an absent effect, and stops on a conflict or indeterminate result.
58	57 │   - A receipt records the evidence collected.
59	58 │ 
60	59 │ Release operations follow known dependency and platform prerequisites. They do not follow a fixed Cargo, npm, then PyPI sequence. The [release guide](releasing.md) covers the local and CI paths, retries, and recovery.
61	60 │ 
62	61 │ ## Current support
63	62 │ 
64	63 │ Callisto is pre-v1. These rows describe current behavior rather than planned adapters.
65	64 │ 
66	65 │ | Ecosystem | Versioning | Publishing |
67	66 │ | --- | --- | --- |
68	67 │ | Cargo | Crate versions, supported dependency declarations, lockfiles | Cargo |
69	68 │ | npm/pnpm | Package versions, supported native dependency forms, lockfiles | Native npm tooling |
70	69 │ | Python/PyPI | Static PEP 621 or Poetry versions | Build backend and Twine |
71	70 │ 
72	71 │ | Layout | Current boundary |
73	72 │ | --- | --- |
74	73 │ | Cargo product binaries | Generated CI builds discovered Cargo binary targets. Other products need a user authored builder. |
75	74 │ | napi platform packages | Generated CI supports configured targets and builds only the packages in the release. |
76	75 │ | Co-located Cargo and Maturin | Discovery fails; no generated Maturin workflow. |
77	76 │ | Custom product assets | Declared artifact slots can use a manual CI builder and Callisto's execute route. |
78	77 │ 
79	78 │ Known release limits matter when choosing a workflow:
80	79 │ 
81	80 │ - A multi-registry release is not atomic.
82	81 │ - Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Go and NuGet publishers are not available.
83	82 │ 
84	83 │ Package owners control native lifecycle hooks. Callisto invokes supported tools without rewriting those hooks. See [publishing](publishing.md) for credentials and Python index limits, and [releasing](releasing.md) for the complete operation and recovery rules.
85	=== docs/releasing.md
86	  1 │ # Releasing
87	  2 │ 
88	  3 │ How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.
89	  4 │ 
90	  5 │ For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).
91	  6 │ 
92	  7 │ ---
93	  8 │ 
94	  9 │ ## Local release: `callisto release`
95	 10 │ 
96	 11 │ `callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.
97	 12 │ 
98	 13 │ - `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
99	 14 │ - `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
100	 15 │ - It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
101	 16 │ - It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
102	 17 │ - It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
103	 18 │ - A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.
104	 19 │ 
105	 20 │ `cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.
106	 21 │ 
107	 22 │ ### Current retry limit
108	 23 │ 
109	 24 │ If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.
110	 25 │ 
111	 26 │ - `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
112	 27 │ - Generated simple workflows share this limit.
113	 28 │ - CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.
114	 29 │ 
115	 30 │ ---
116	 31 │ 
117	 32 │ ## Generated workflows
118	 33 │ 
119	 34 │ `callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.
120	 35 │ 
121	 36 │ Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.
122	 37 │ 
123	 38 │ - **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
124	 39 │ - **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
125	 40 │ - Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.
126	 41 │ 
127	 42 │ Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).
128	 43 │ 
129	 44 │ Generated build support has these boundaries:
130	 45 │ 
131	 46 │ - Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
132	 47 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
133	 48 │ - Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
134	 49 │ - Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.
135	 50 │ 
136	 51 │ The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.
137	 52 │ 
138	 53 │ Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.
139	 54 │ 
140	 55 │ Build-matrix limits:
141	 56 │ 
142	 57 │ - An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
143	 58 │ - Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
144	 59 │ - Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
145	 60 │ - The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
146	 61 │ - Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.
147	 62 │ 
148	 63 │ ---
149	 64 │ 
150	 65 │ ## Release PR and approval
151	 66 │ 
152	 67 │ The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.
153	 68 │ 
154	 69 │ The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
155	 70 │ 
156	 71 │ Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.
157	 72 │ 
158	 73 │ After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.
159	 74 │ 
160	 75 │ ## PR pre-flight verification
161	 76 │ 
162	 77 │ [`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:
163	 78 │ 
164	 79 │ - `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
165	 80 │ - `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
166	 81 │ - Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.
167	 82 │ 
168	 83 │ ---
169	 84 │ 
170	 85 │ ## Release identity and recovery
171	 86 │ 
172	 87 │ Every release run records two different revisions:
173	 88 │ 
174	 89 │ - The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
175	 90 │ - The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.
176	 91 │ 
177	 92 │ A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.
178	 93 │ 
179	 94 │ To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.
180	 95 │ 
181	 96 │ Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.
182	 97 │ 
183	 98 │ ## Recovering an older release
184	 99 │ 
185	100 │ Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:
186	101 │ 
187	102 │ **E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:
188	103 │ 
189	104 │ ```sh
190	105 │ SHA=<release-source sha>
191	106 │ git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
192	107 │ git push origin "<tag>"
193	108 │ gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
194	109 │ ```
195	110 │ 
196	111 │ **`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:
197	112 │ 
198	113 │ ```sh
199	114 │ gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
200	115 │ gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
201	116 │ ```
202	117 │ 
203	118 │ ## Publication checks
204	119 │ 
205	120 │ Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.
206	121 │ 
207	122 │ Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
208	123 │ 
209	124 │ GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.
210	125 │ 
211	126 │ ---
212	127 │ 
213	128 │ ## Platform-package publish order
214	129 │ 
215	130 │ `callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.
216	131 │ 
217	132 │ A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.
218	133 │ 
219	134 │ - **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
220	135 │ - **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.
221	136 │ 
222	137 │ For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
223	=== docs/publishing.md
224	  1 │ # Publishing: registry authentication
225	  2 │ 
226	  3 │ Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).
227	  4 │ 
228	  5 │ Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.
229	  6 │ 
230	  7 │ ---
231	  8 │ 
232	  9 │ ## npm
233	 10 │ 
234	 11 │ Two supported patterns.
235	 12 │ 
236	 13 │ ### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
237	 14 │ 
238	 15 │ Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
239	 16 │ 
240	 17 │ ```yaml
241	 18 │ - name: Authenticate with npm registry
242	 19 │   run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
243	 20 │   env:
244	 21 │     NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
245	 22 │ 
246	 23 │ - run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
247	 24 │ ```
248	 25 │ 
249	 26 │ `npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
250	 27 │ 
251	 28 │ ### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
252	 29 │ 
253	 30 │ `actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
254	 31 │ 
255	 32 │ ```yaml
256	 33 │ - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
257	 34 │   with:
258	 35 │     node-version: '20'
259	 36 │     registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
260	 37 │ 
261	 38 │ - run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
262	 39 │   env:
263	 40 │     NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
264	 41 │ ```
265	 42 │ 
266	 43 │ `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
267	 44 │ 
268	 45 │ ### Choosing a pattern
269	 46 │ 
270	 47 │ | Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
271	 48 │ | --- | --- | --- |
272	 49 │ | Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
273	 50 │ | Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
274	 51 │ | Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
275	 52 │ | Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
276	 53 │ 
277	 54 │ ### Provenance
278	 55 │ 
279	 56 │ Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
280	 57 │ 
281	 58 │ ---
282	 59 │ 
283	 60 │ ## Cargo (crates.io)
284	 61 │ 
285	 62 │ Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
286	 63 │ 
287	 64 │ ```yaml
288	 65 │ env:
289	 66 │   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
290	 67 │ ```
291	 68 │ 
292	 69 │ Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.
293	 70 │ 
294	 71 │ ---
295	 72 │ 
296	 73 │ ## Python (PyPI)
297	 74 │ 
298	 75 │ Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
299	 76 │ 
300	 77 │ ```yaml
301	 78 │ env:
302	 79 │   TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
303	 80 │   TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
304	 81 │ ```
305	 82 │ 
306	 83 │ Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.
307	 84 │ 
308	 85 │ The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.
309	 86 │ 
310	 87 │ ### Generated Callisto workflows
311	 88 │ 
312	 89 │ Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
313	 90 │ 
314	 91 │ Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.
315	 92 │ 
316	 93 │ ### Current Python support limits
317	 94 │ 
318	 95 │ Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:
319	 96 │ 
320	 97 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
321	 98 │ - Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
322	 99 │ - A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
323	100 │ - A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
324	101 │ - A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
325	102 │ - A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
326	103 │ - Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
327	104 │ - Snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI rejects. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
328	=== docs/config.md
329	  1 │ # Configuration reference
330	  2 │ 
331	  3 │ Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).
332	  4 │ 
333	  5 │ This reference describes current keys, not the [proposed canonical-identity/polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Exact references can currently be bare or qualified; prefer `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` and `pypi/name` when writing new configuration. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration is implemented yet.
334	  6 │ 
335	  7 │ ## Top-level tables
336	  8 │ 
337	  9 │ | Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
338	 10 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
339	 11 │ | `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
340	 12 │ | `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
341	 13 │ | `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
342	 14 │ | `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
343	 15 │ | `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
344	 16 │ | `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
345	 17 │ | `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
346	 18 │ | `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
347	 19 │ | `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
348	 20 │ | `[init]` | table | no | Deprecated; parsed for compatibility, never read |
349	 21 │ 
350	 22 │ ## `[changesets]`
351	 23 │ 
352	 24 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
353	 25 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
354	 26 │ | `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |
355	 27 │ 
356	 28 │ Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.
357	 29 │ 
358	 30 │ ## `[cascade]`
359	 31 │ 
360	 32 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
361	 33 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
362	 34 │ | `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
363	 35 │ | `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
364	 36 │ | `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
365	 37 │ | `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |
366	 38 │ 
367	 39 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
368	 40 │ ```toml
369	 41 │ [cascade]
370	 42 │ mode = "out-of-range"
371	 43 │ bump-severity = "patch"
372	 44 │ peer-escalation = true
373	 45 │ preserve-npm-ranges = true
374	 46 │ ```
375	 47 │ 
376	 48 │ ## `[validation]`
377	 49 │ 
378	 50 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
379	 51 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
380	 52 │ | `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |
381	 53 │ 
382	 54 │ ## `[release]`
383	 55 │ 
384	 56 │ Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.
385	 57 │ 
386	 58 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
387	 59 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
388	 60 │ | `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
389	 61 │ | `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
390	 62 │ | `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
391	 63 │ | `[release.profiles]` | table | none | Legacy; only `profiles.production` is read, to migrate its `forge-repository` into the top-level key. Conflicting values between the two are a hard error. |
392	 64 │ 
393	 65 │ ### `[[release.artifact]]`
394	 66 │ 
395	 67 │ | Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
396	 68 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
397	 69 │ | `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
398	 70 │ | `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
399	 71 │ | `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |
400	 72 │ 
401	 73 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
402	 74 │ ```toml
403	 75 │ [release]
404	 76 │ product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
405	 77 │ forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"
406	 78 │ 
407	 79 │ [[release.artifact]]
408	 80 │ package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
409	 81 │ target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
410	 82 │ asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
411	 83 │ ```
412	 84 │ 
413	 85 │ ## `[registries]`
414	 86 │ 
415	 87 │ Keyed by registry name. Three registries are built in, keyed `cratesIo` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). `cratesIo` and `npm` exist with no URL override even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<built-in>]` entry changes their settings and may leave `kind` out.
416	 88 │ 
417	 89 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
418	 90 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
419	 91 │ | `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
420	 92 │ | `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
421	 93 │ | `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
422	 94 │ | `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
423	 95 │ | `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |
424	 96 │ 
425	 97 │ For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.
426	 98 │ 
427	 99 │ Example:
428	100 │ ```toml
429	101 │ [registries.internal-npm]
430	102 │ kind = "npm"
431	103 │ url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
432	104 │ ```
433	105 │ 
434	106 │ ## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`
435	107 │ 
436	108 │ Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.
437	109 │ 
438	110 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
439	111 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
440	112 │ | `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. A name without its ecosystem is E317. |
441	113 │ | `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
442	114 │ | `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
443	115 │ | `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
444	116 │ | `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
445	117 │ | `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
446	118 │ | `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |
447	119 │ 
448	120 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
449	121 │ ```toml
450	122 │ [[package]]
451	123 │ match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
452	124 │ publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
453	125 │ tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
454	126 │ previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
455	127 │ ```
456	128 │ 
457	129 │ ## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`
458	130 │ 
459	131 │ Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.
460	132 │ 
461	133 │ | Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
462	134 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
463	135 │ | `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
464	136 │ | `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |
465	137 │ 
466	138 │ `[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.
467	139 │ 
468	140 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
469	141 │ ```toml
470	142 │ [[fixed-group]]
471	143 │ name = "workspace"
472	144 │ members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli"]
473	145 │ ```
474	146 │ 
475	147 │ ## `[init]`
476	148 │ 
477	149 │ Deprecated. `ecosystems` (array of strings) is parsed so older config files still load, but nothing reads it.
478	150 │ 
479	151 │ ## Identity and defaults
480	152 │ 
481	153 │ Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.

=== docs/how-callisto-works.md
 1 │ # How Callisto works
 2 │ 
 3 │ Callisto turns changesets and native package metadata into a version plan. It then coordinates the selected registry, Git, and GitHub operations. Current scope is Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI.
 4 │ 
 5 │ ## Where it fits
 6 │ 
 7 │ Use Callisto when contributors should declare release impact and a repo needs native dependency updates across its supported package types. The version plan makes each bump reviewable before publication.
 8 │ 
 9 │ Other tools may fit your existing workflow:
10 │ 
11 │ - [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) focuses on npm package releases.
12 │ - [Knope](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) offers configurable release workflows.
13 │ - [Nx Release](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases) integrates with Nx projects and tasks.
14 │ - [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/design.md) builds release PRs from conventional commits.
15 │ 
16 │ ## A change through the system
17 │ 
18 │ Suppose a Cargo crate `service` depends on `core`. A contributor records a change to `core`:
19 │ 
20 │ ```sh
21 │ callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API"
22 │ callisto status
23 │ callisto version --dry-run
24 │ ```
25 │ 
26 │ Callisto builds the version plan from the changeset, manifests, and `callisto.toml`:
27 │ 
28 │ - The changeset requests a minor bump for `core`.
29 │ - The Cargo dependency in `service` tells Callisto whether the new version fits its existing requirement.
30 │   - Under the default `out-of-range` policy, a version outside that requirement can bump `service` and update its dependency declaration.
31 │   - Cascade mode and bump severity are configurable.
32 │ - Fixed and linked groups can add packages through explicit policy.
33 │ - Unrelated npm and Python packages do not join solely because they share the repo.
34 │ 
35 │ After reviewing the plan, `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs. It stages the versioned state for a commit. `callisto release --dry-run` then previews the release operations.
36 │ 
37 │ ## The model
38 │ 
39 │ | Concept | What it means today |
40 │ | --- | --- |
41 │ | Workspace package | A dependency graph node located from source and manifests. |
42 │ | Distribution | A native Cargo, npm, or PyPI identity described by a manifest. One package can expose multiple supported distributions. |
43 │ | Native dependency | A manifest relationship that can affect dependent versions and publication order. |
44 │ | Version group | An explicit fixed or linked rule in `callisto.toml`. |
45 │ | Release operation | One registry, tag, GitHub release, or asset effect with prerequisites. |
46 │ 
47 │ These relationships serve different purposes. For example, a Rust library embedded in a Python wheel is a build input. That alone does not create a Cargo registry dependency or make the crate and wheel share a version. See [configuration](config.md) for supported dependency and version-group rules.
48 │ 
49 │ ## Releasing and recovery
50 │ 
51 │ - **Local release:** `callisto release --dry-run` previews the plan. `callisto release` runs it from a clean checkout.
52 │   - Native publishers use their own credentials.
53 │ - **Managed CI:** The version PR commits the selected package and version decision. CI verifies it after merge.
54 │   - Planning declares operations. Building creates artifacts. Execution receives registry credentials.
55 │ - **Execution:** Callisto checks each provider before acting.
56 │   - It adopts an exact match, performs and confirms an absent effect, and stops on a conflict or indeterminate result.
57 │   - A receipt records the evidence collected.
58 │ 
59 │ Release operations follow known dependency and platform prerequisites. They do not follow a fixed Cargo, npm, then PyPI sequence. The [release guide](releasing.md) covers the local and CI paths, retries, and recovery.
60 │ 
61 │ ## Current support
62 │ 
63 │ Callisto is pre-v1. These rows describe current behavior rather than planned adapters.
64 │ 
65 │ | Ecosystem | Versioning | Publishing |
66 │ | --- | --- | --- |
67 │ | Cargo | Crate versions, supported dependency declarations, lockfiles | Cargo |
68 │ | npm/pnpm | Package versions, supported native dependency forms, lockfiles | Native npm tooling |
69 │ | Python/PyPI | Static PEP 621 or Poetry versions | Build backend and Twine |
70 │ 
71 │ | Layout | Current boundary |
72 │ | --- | --- |
73 │ | Cargo product binaries | Generated CI builds discovered Cargo binary targets. Other products need a user authored builder. |
74 │ | napi platform packages | Generated CI supports configured targets and builds only the packages in the release. |
75 │ | Co-located Cargo and Maturin | Discovery fails; no generated Maturin workflow. |
76 │ | Custom product assets | Declared artifact slots can use a manual CI builder and Callisto's execute route. |
77 │ 
78 │ Known release limits matter when choosing a workflow:
79 │ 
80 │ - A multi-registry release is not atomic.
81 │ - Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Go and NuGet publishers are not available.
82 │ 
83 │ Package owners control native lifecycle hooks. Callisto invokes supported tools without rewriting those hooks. See [publishing](publishing.md) for credentials and Python index limits, and [releasing](releasing.md) for the complete operation and recovery rules.
=== docs/releasing.md
  1 │ # Releasing
  2 │ 
  3 │ How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.
  4 │ 
  5 │ For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).
  6 │ 
  7 │ ---
  8 │ 
  9 │ ## Local release: `callisto release`
 10 │ 
 11 │ `callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.
 12 │ 
 13 │ - `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
 14 │ - `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
 15 │ - It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
 16 │ - It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
 17 │ - It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
 18 │ - A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.
 19 │ 
 20 │ `cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.
 21 │ 
 22 │ ### Current retry limit
 23 │ 
 24 │ If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.
 25 │ 
 26 │ - `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
 27 │ - Generated simple workflows share this limit.
 28 │ - CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.
 29 │ 
 30 │ ---
 31 │ 
 32 │ ## Generated workflows
 33 │ 
 34 │ `callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.
 35 │ 
 36 │ Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.
 37 │ 
 38 │ - **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
 39 │ - **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
 40 │ - Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.
 41 │ 
 42 │ Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).
 43 │ 
 44 │ Generated build support has these boundaries:
 45 │ 
 46 │ - Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
 47 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
 48 │ - Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
 49 │ - Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.
 50 │ 
 51 │ The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.
 52 │ 
 53 │ Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.
 54 │ 
 55 │ Build-matrix limits:
 56 │ 
 57 │ - An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
 58 │ - Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
 59 │ - Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
 60 │ - The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
 61 │ - Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.
 62 │ 
 63 │ ---
 64 │ 
 65 │ ## Release PR and approval
 66 │ 
 67 │ The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.
 68 │ 
 69 │ The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
 70 │ 
 71 │ Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.
 72 │ 
 73 │ After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.
 74 │ 
 75 │ ## PR pre-flight verification
 76 │ 
 77 │ [`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:
 78 │ 
 79 │ - `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
 80 │ - `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
 81 │ - Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.
 82 │ 
 83 │ ---
 84 │ 
 85 │ ## Release identity and recovery
 86 │ 
 87 │ Every release run records two different revisions:
 88 │ 
 89 │ - The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
 90 │ - The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.
 91 │ 
 92 │ A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.
 93 │ 
 94 │ To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.
 95 │ 
 96 │ Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.
 97 │ 
 98 │ ## Recovering an older release
 99 │ 
100 │ Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:
101 │ 
102 │ **E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:
103 │ 
104 │ ```sh
105 │ SHA=<release-source sha>
106 │ git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
107 │ git push origin "<tag>"
108 │ gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
109 │ ```
110 │ 
111 │ **`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:
112 │ 
113 │ ```sh
114 │ gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
115 │ gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
116 │ ```
117 │ 
118 │ ## Publication checks
119 │ 
120 │ Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.
121 │ 
122 │ Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
123 │ 
124 │ GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.
125 │ 
126 │ ---
127 │ 
128 │ ## Platform-package publish order
129 │ 
130 │ `callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.
131 │ 
132 │ A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.
133 │ 
134 │ - **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
135 │ - **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.
136 │ 
137 │ For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
=== docs/publishing.md
  1 │ # Publishing: registry authentication
  2 │ 
  3 │ Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).
  4 │ 
  5 │ Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.
  6 │ 
  7 │ ---
  8 │ 
  9 │ ## npm
 10 │ 
 11 │ Two supported patterns.
 12 │ 
 13 │ ### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
 14 │ 
 15 │ Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
 16 │ 
 17 │ ```yaml
 18 │ - name: Authenticate with npm registry
 19 │   run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
 20 │   env:
 21 │     NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
 22 │ 
 23 │ - run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
 24 │ ```
 25 │ 
 26 │ `npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
 27 │ 
 28 │ ### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
 29 │ 
 30 │ `actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
 31 │ 
 32 │ ```yaml
 33 │ - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
 34 │   with:
 35 │     node-version: '20'
 36 │     registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
 37 │ 
 38 │ - run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
 39 │   env:
 40 │     NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
 41 │ ```
 42 │ 
 43 │ `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
 44 │ 
 45 │ ### Choosing a pattern
 46 │ 
 47 │ | Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
 48 │ | --- | --- | --- |
 49 │ | Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
 50 │ | Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
 51 │ | Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
 52 │ | Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
 53 │ 
 54 │ ### Provenance
 55 │ 
 56 │ Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
 57 │ 
 58 │ ---
 59 │ 
 60 │ ## Cargo (crates.io)
 61 │ 
 62 │ Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
 63 │ 
 64 │ ```yaml
 65 │ env:
 66 │   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
 67 │ ```
 68 │ 
 69 │ Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.
 70 │ 
 71 │ ---
 72 │ 
 73 │ ## Python (PyPI)
 74 │ 
 75 │ Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
 76 │ 
 77 │ ```yaml
 78 │ env:
 79 │   TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
 80 │   TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
 81 │ ```
 82 │ 
 83 │ Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.
 84 │ 
 85 │ The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.
 86 │ 
 87 │ ### Generated Callisto workflows
 88 │ 
 89 │ Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
 90 │ 
 91 │ Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.
 92 │ 
 93 │ ### Current Python support limits
 94 │ 
 95 │ Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:
 96 │ 
 97 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
 98 │ - Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
 99 │ - A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
100 │ - A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
101 │ - A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
102 │ - A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
103 │ - Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
104 │ - Snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI rejects. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
=== docs/config.md
  1 │ # Configuration reference
  2 │ 
  3 │ Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).
  4 │ 
  5 │ This reference describes current keys, not the [proposed canonical-identity/polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Exact references can currently be bare or qualified; prefer `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` and `pypi/name` when writing new configuration. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration is implemented yet.
  6 │ 
  7 │ ## Top-level tables
  8 │ 
  9 │ | Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
 10 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 11 │ | `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
 12 │ | `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
 13 │ | `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
 14 │ | `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
 15 │ | `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
 16 │ | `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
 17 │ | `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
 18 │ | `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
 19 │ | `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
 20 │ | `[init]` | table | no | Deprecated; parsed for compatibility, never read |
 21 │ 
 22 │ ## `[changesets]`
 23 │ 
 24 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
 25 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 26 │ | `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |
 27 │ 
 28 │ Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.
 29 │ 
 30 │ ## `[cascade]`
 31 │ 
 32 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
 33 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 34 │ | `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
 35 │ | `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
 36 │ | `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
 37 │ | `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |
 38 │ 
 39 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
 40 │ ```toml
 41 │ [cascade]
 42 │ mode = "out-of-range"
 43 │ bump-severity = "patch"
 44 │ peer-escalation = true
 45 │ preserve-npm-ranges = true
 46 │ ```
 47 │ 
 48 │ ## `[validation]`
 49 │ 
 50 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
 51 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 52 │ | `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |
 53 │ 
 54 │ ## `[release]`
 55 │ 
 56 │ Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.
 57 │ 
 58 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
 59 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 60 │ | `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
 61 │ | `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
 62 │ | `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
 63 │ | `[release.profiles]` | table | none | Legacy; only `profiles.production` is read, to migrate its `forge-repository` into the top-level key. Conflicting values between the two are a hard error. |
 64 │ 
 65 │ ### `[[release.artifact]]`
 66 │ 
 67 │ | Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
 68 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 69 │ | `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
 70 │ | `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
 71 │ | `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |
 72 │ 
 73 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
 74 │ ```toml
 75 │ [release]
 76 │ product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
 77 │ forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"
 78 │ 
 79 │ [[release.artifact]]
 80 │ package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
 81 │ target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
 82 │ asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
 83 │ ```
 84 │ 
 85 │ ## `[registries]`
 86 │ 
 87 │ Keyed by registry name. Three registries are built in, keyed `cratesIo` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). `cratesIo` and `npm` exist with no URL override even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<built-in>]` entry changes their settings and may leave `kind` out.
 88 │ 
 89 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
 90 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 91 │ | `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
 92 │ | `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
 93 │ | `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
 94 │ | `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
 95 │ | `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |
 96 │ 
 97 │ For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.
 98 │ 
 99 │ Example:
100 │ ```toml
101 │ [registries.internal-npm]
102 │ kind = "npm"
103 │ url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
104 │ ```
105 │ 
106 │ ## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`
107 │ 
108 │ Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.
109 │ 
110 │ | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
111 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
112 │ | `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. A name without its ecosystem is E317. |
113 │ | `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
114 │ | `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
115 │ | `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
116 │ | `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
117 │ | `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
118 │ | `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |
119 │ 
120 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
121 │ ```toml
122 │ [[package]]
123 │ match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
124 │ publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
125 │ tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
126 │ previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
127 │ ```
128 │ 
129 │ ## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`
130 │ 
131 │ Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.
132 │ 
133 │ | Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
134 │ | --- | --- | --- | --- |
135 │ | `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
136 │ | `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |
137 │ 
138 │ `[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.
139 │ 
140 │ Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
141 │ ```toml
142 │ [[fixed-group]]
143 │ name = "workspace"
144 │ members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli"]
145 │ ```
146 │ 
147 │ ## `[init]`
148 │ 
149 │ Deprecated. `ecosystems` (array of strings) is parsed so older config files still load, but nothing reads it.
150 │ 
151 │ ## Identity and defaults
152 │ 
153 │ Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.

Usage: callisto release [OPTIONS]

Options:

      --cwd <CWD>                 Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory) [default: .]

      --package <ECOSYSTEM/NAME>  Release this qualified package, for example `cargo/callisto-cli`, with every distribution of it and the members of its groups. Repeatable
      --receipt <FILE>            Also write the release receipt to this file

Usage: callisto version [OPTIONS]

Options:

          Output format for command results
          
          [default: text]
          [possible values: text, json]

      --cwd <CWD>
          Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory)
          
          [default: .]

      --no-refresh-lockfiles
          Skip regenerating lockfiles after applying the version bumps

      --dry-run
          Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk

      --strict
          Treat warning-level diagnostics as errors

      --allow-empty-changesets
          Allow versioning to proceed even if no changesets are pending

      --emit-decision <PATH>
          Writes the exact release decision this version plan authorizes -- package, target version, and inclusion reason (changeset, fixed group, linked group, dependency cascade, or pre-release policy) -- to the given path, alongside the manifest and changelog edits.

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
